question: May a verification finding whose evidencePaths are ALL documentation prose (.md / .rst / .txt) be capped at Minor, so it records as a nit instead of opening a metered re-verify round?
decision: Approved and implemented as the spec's literal rule: is_blocking_issue caps a finding at Minor when it names at least one evidence path and EVERY named path is documentation prose. The cap is uniform across declared severities (Critical and Major alike), matching spec step 4. Three guards keep it from becoming a laundering vector: (1) doc-ness is derived from the paths only, never from the verifier's self-description or category; (2) a finding with NO evidencePaths is unchanged - unknown still blocks; (3) behaviour-bearing markdown (ai_router/prompt-templates/**) is explicitly NOT documentation, because those files are the verifier's own instructions and a defect in them changes routed behaviour.

options.option: Cap doc-only findings at Minor for every declared severity (the spec's literal step-4 rule). CHOSEN.
options.consequence: A wording complaint about a .md file records as a nit and opens no round. Set 116 S3 evidence: 13 routed calls / $4.75, code clean from round 1, every Critical/Major after round 1 concerned the wording of docs/session-constitution.md, and two of the three were created by fixing the previous one. Residual risk: a genuinely Critical doc defect (e.g. a runbook that instructs a destructive command) records as a nit rather than blocking; it is still surfaced to the orchestrator in the same round, so the risk is 'not forced to fix now', not 'not seen'. Historically Critical is 3 of 572 findings.

options.option: Cap only Major; leave Critical doc-only findings blocking.
options.consequence: Keeps a blocking path for a catastrophic doc defect, at the cost of a second severity rule to maintain and a new incentive for a verifier to reach for Critical to keep its wording complaint alive - the laundering vector running in reverse. Buys little: Critical is 3 of 572 findings historically, and none of Set 116 S3's churn was Critical.

options.option: No cap - keep every Critical/Major blocking regardless of evidence (status quo).
options.consequence: Preserves today's severity semantics exactly, and leaves the measured churn in place: 520 of 572 findings (91%) are Major, so a scale on which 91% of findings block is not a scale, and documentation wording keeps buying ~$0.88 rounds. The spec exists because this was measured, not estimated.

operator_attestation: Operator, in-session on 2026-08-10, before any cap code was written: 'When you get to step #3, you have my attestation here to continue, overriding the block on a verification reduction.' The operator authorized capping doc-only findings at Minor per spec step 4 of docs/session-sets/119-close-preflight-and-doc-only-findings/spec.md, having set the measurements the spec records. The reduction is bounded to findings whose own cited evidence is entirely documentation prose; nothing is deleted or hidden - a capped finding is still recorded and still reported to the orchestrator, it simply does not buy a routed round.
evidence: Set 116 S3: 13 routed calls, $4.75; code clean at round 1 and stayed clean; the session's one real code defect was caught by the test suite before verification ran; two of the three Major findings that followed were introduced by fixing the previous one.
572 findings across this repo's history: 520 Major (91%), 3 Critical, 21 Minor.
category cannot substitute for a path: it is free text and across all 572 findings reads 'docs' twice and 'documentation' once.
reversal_path: Delete the DOC_EVIDENCE_SUFFIXES branch from ai_router.verification.is_blocking_issue (one predicate call at one chokepoint); the two falsifiers in ai_router/tests/test_doc_only_cap.py then fail, naming the removal.

question: The spec's Touches list for Session 2 does not name close_backstop.py, but its step 2 requires the preflight to evaluate the close's predicates 'by calling them rather than re-implementing them', and the expensive case (step 3) is the backstop's own skip-vs-run decision. Copy that decision into close_preflight.py, or extract it from run_close_backstop so both callers share one spelling?
decision: Extracted. close_backstop.decide_backstop (+ the BackstopDecision dataclass) now holds the whole pre-metered sequence -- disposition/session presence, method-token vocabulary, budget.yaml zero-budget tier, orchestrator identity, settling stamped evidence, the classic round bound, and the git diff base -- and run_close_backstop calls it, using the returned identity / round_number / diff_base for the half that actually spends money. close_preflight calls the same function. run_close_backstop's observable behaviour is unchanged (its 51 existing tests pass untouched), and the branch ORDER, which is load-bearing, is preserved exactly: the round bound is still evaluated AFTER the settling-evidence skip, so a session that ran a long loop and then verified clean still closes.

options.option: Extract the decision into a shared function and have both callers use it. CHOSEN.
options.consequence: One spelling, two readers, so the preflight cannot drift from the close it predicts. Costs an edit to a file the spec's Touches list does not name, and touches a module Session 3 will also edit (for the backstop baseline record) -- but that is sequential, not concurrent, and the extraction actually helps Session 3 by separating the decision from the execution it needs to change.

options.option: Re-implement the seven-branch sequence inside close_preflight.py, leaving close_backstop.py untouched.
options.consequence: Obeys the Touches list literally and creates exactly the two-spellings-of-one-rule drift L-066-1 and L-069-1 exist to prevent. The sequence's ORDER is load-bearing and undocumented in any single place, so the copy would be subtly wrong the first time either file moved -- and a preflight that disagrees with the gate is worse than no preflight, because it teaches orchestrators to distrust it. Rejected.

options.option: Answer only the cheap questions (git preconditions, disposition, test-run freshness) and skip the backstop prediction entirely.
options.consequence: Obeys the Touches list AND avoids the duplication, at the cost of the session's whole point: verification_backstop is 79 of 214 recorded check-failures and the only one that spends a routed call at close time. Spec step 3 names it explicitly as the case that must be covered. Rejected.

evidence: Spec step 2: the preflight 'evaluates the same predicates the close evaluates, by calling them rather than re-implementing them'. Spec step 3 names the backstop as the case worth 78 (measured today: 79) of the still-blocking historical failures. project-guidance.md -> Code Style: a pure-Python validator mirroring another contract must hold parity in BOTH directions (L-066-1); a bug is a bug CLASS, fix every sibling site (L-069-1). ai_router/tests/test_close_backstop.py: 51 tests pass unchanged after the extraction.
reversal_path: Inline decide_backstop back into run_close_backstop and give close_preflight its own copy. The dataclass and function are additive; nothing else imports them except close_preflight.

question: The verification loop reached its enforced bound (2 discovery passes + 2 remediation-review cycles) with one Major from round 4 fixed but unreviewed: --session-number now accepts-and-checks the caller's assertion instead of being removed. Settle it by adjudication, or authorize one more remediation-review round to review the fix delta?
decision: Operator authorized exactly ONE more remediation-review round to review the fix delta. Not an acceptance of the finding's dismissal and not a licence to grind: the authorization covers one round, and if it returns a fresh blocking finding the loop stops to the operator again rather than continuing.

options.option: Authorize one more remediation-review round to review the fix delta. CHOSEN.
options.consequence: Costs one routed call (on this Copilot CLI seat, billed usage is unavailable and cost_usd records 0.0). Buys cross-provider review of a public-CLI contract change that landed AFTER the reviewer's last look. The last two rounds each found that a fix introduced a NEW problem -- round 3's two findings were both created by round 1's fix -- which is precisely the pattern this set's own spec documents, and it is the argument against self-certifying this one.

options.option: Adjudicate it settled now on the executable-criterion evidence and close on the operator-attested --manual-verify path.
options.consequence: Faster and free. The finding's own acceptance criterion passes verbatim (exit 1, "session_number": 2) and 59 tests pass, so the evidence is real -- but the acceptance harness explicitly REFUSED to auto-close it (its only pre-fix tree belongs to round 2, so a fails-before result would not be attributable to this fix). Shipping a public-CLI semantic change with no cross-provider look would be an owed residual with a named owner. Rejected in favour of one confirming round.

options.option: Third-provider opinion on just this finding.
options.consequence: Appropriate when a finding is DISPUTED. This one is not: the orchestrator accepted it and fixed it. A third opinion would arbitrate a disagreement that does not exist, at the same cost as reviewing the actual fix. Rejected.

options.option: Revert to removing --session-number and dismiss round 4's finding on operator adjudication.
options.consequence: Defensible on the letter -- close_session itself has no session flag -- but it discards a fix that satisfies BOTH round-1 finding 4 (no mixed-session report is representable) and round-4's finding (the spec's promised input works). Reverting to make a finding go away is the wrong direction. Rejected.

operator_attestation: Operator authorized one additional remediation-review round for Set 119 Session 2 on 2026-08-10, after an education-mode brief naming the bound reached, the single fixed-but-unreviewed Major, the passing executable acceptance criterion, and the acceptance harness's baseline-mismatch refusal. The authorization is for one round to review the fix delta; it does not pre-approve any further round.
evidence: s2-rounds.jsonl records 4 completed rounds (discovery, supplementary, remediation-review x2), all ISSUES_FOUND/blocking. Round 4 recorded 'fix verdicts: 6 accepted, 1 rejected'. acceptance_harness --round 4: 0 auto-closed, reason 'baseline-mismatch: the only pre-fix tree available belongs to an earlier round than the one that raised this finding'. The finding's executable criterion run verbatim returns exit 1 with "session_number": 2. ai_router/tests/test_close_preflight.py: 59 passing.
reversal_path: The authorization is spent by the single round it licenses; nothing persists. If that round returns a blocking finding, the loop stops to the operator again -- a further round would need a further attestation.

question: Round 5 returned VERIFIED, but the mandated close-time `cite_lessons` write bumped three `last-used-set` metadata trailers in docs/planning/lessons-learned.md and lessons-archive.md, staling the stamp's work_diff_sha256. The close backstop would normally re-verify, but the round budget is spent so it refuses. Close on the operator-attested --manual-verify path, or authorize another round?
decision: Operator authorized close on the --manual-verify path, attesting round 5's evidence. The verification is real and current in substance: round 5 (gpt-5.5, effective provider openai, cross-provider against an anthropic orchestrator) returned VERIFIED with 8/8 fix verdicts accepted and zero findings, and `git diff` proves the ENTIRE post-round-5 content delta is three metadata trailer lines written by cite_lessons. No source, test, schema or prose changed after the round. A fresh round would re-review byte-identical work.

options.consequence: Closes on an operator attestation rather than a machine-validated stamp -- a real, if narrow, reduction in corroboration. Narrow because the attestation names a routed cross-provider round that actually ran, whose raw artifact is on disk, and whose reviewed content is provably identical to what is being closed. The residual is that the close-time evidence check is satisfied by a human statement instead of a hash.

options.option: Authorize one more verification round to produce a stamp bound to the committed tree.
options.consequence: Yields genuine settling evidence instead of an attestation, at one routed call (billed 0.0 on this Copilot CLI seat). Rejected as waste: the round would re-review code that has not changed by a single character since the round that already passed it, and the loop's own rule is that persisting past a bound requires a MATERIAL Critical/Major -- a metadata trailer is not one.

options.option: Add the guidance files to WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING now, then re-verify.
options.consequence: Fixes the framework gap at its root, but edits verification-integrity machinery after the tree was frozen and the run of record was taken, so it would invalidate both and need its own round. Wrong session for it. Recorded as an owed finding for Session 3, which already touches close_backstop.py and the stamp machinery.

options.option: Revert the cite_lessons bump, close, re-cite afterwards.
options.consequence: Restores the stamp with no routed call, and is the worst option: it defeats the citation-at-close contract that the whole guidance-archival signal depends on, and it would make the ledger say a lesson was not used when it was. Rejected.

operator_attestation: Operator attests the Set 119 Session 2 close on 2026-08-11 after an education-mode brief. Verifying surface: `python -m ai_router.verify_session --phase remediation-review`, round 5, operator-authorized past the bound. Verifier model gpt-5.5, effective provider openai, cross-provider against the anthropic orchestrator (claude-opus-5 on a Copilot CLI seat). Template: the pinned session-verification template. Verdict: VERIFIED, 8 of 8 fix verdicts accepted, zero findings. Raw artifact: docs/session-sets/119-close-preflight-and-doc-only-findings/s2-verification-round-5.md. The stamp is stale for one reason only, verified by `git diff 982e8096~1 982e8096 -- docs/planning/lessons-learned.md docs/planning/lessons-archive.md`: three `last-used-set` metadata trailers bumped by the constitutionally-mandated `cite_lessons` run in the final commit. No source, test, schema or documentation prose changed after round 5. Full suite green on the frozen tree: 3975 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed.
evidence: s2-rounds.jsonl: 5 completed rounds. s2-verification-round-5.md: VERIFIED, 'fix verdicts: 8 accepted, 0 rejected'. The stale-stamp diagnosis is from close_preflight itself, run before the close attempt -- the tool this session shipped caught the problem it exists to catch, one close attempt earlier than the framework otherwise would have. WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING (ai_router/verification_stamp.py) excludes per-set bookkeeping but not the repo-wide guidance files that cite_lessons writes.
reversal_path: None needed; the attestation is recorded in the events ledger by close_session --manual-verify and is auditable. The underlying gap is an owed finding for Session 3: either add the guidance files to WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING, or accept that every citing session pays a backstop round -- which is plausibly a contributor to the 79 verification_backstop firings this session measured.

question: The spec's step 4 names five gate modules as 'unreachable from any close path' and directs deleting them. The proof obligation it sets (no import from a close path, no console-script entry point, no reference in router-config.yaml) fails for three of them. Which of the seven listed modules are actually deleted?
decision: Delete four, keep three, report the discrepancy. DELETED: floor_ratchet.py (no importer anywhere), routed_gate.py (only an __init__ re-export; retired in Set 083 and always exits 0), pricing_proposal.py (no importer), cost_report.py (only __init__ re-exports; its router-config key cost_report_on_exit has no reader in the package). KEPT AND REPORTED: contract_gate.py, because close_session.run calls validate_contract_gate as a live close gate and close_preflight/start_session call it too - it is on the close path the spec says it is off; spec_admission.py, because session_checklist.read_spec_steps calls parse_session_plans to seed the step plan the checklist_posted gate reads; replacement_gate.py, because dual_surface_verify calls validate_benchmark_registration at line 1538 and imports it at module scope, so deleting it would break that module's import outright. The line drawn: a module is REACHABLE when a surviving module CALLS it, and merely being re-exported from __init__.py is publication, not use - which is why routed_gate and cost_report go while replacement_gate stays. Nothing is edited to manufacture unreachability; the spec's own rule is that a reachable module stays and is reported, not forced.

options.option: Delete the four proven-unreachable modules; keep and report the three that are reached. CHOSEN.
options.consequence: The set's stated goal - remove what nothing reaches - is met exactly, and the spec's own escape clause is used as written. Deletion drops far less than the 5,165 LOC the spec predicted, so the 'Ends with' figure is wrong and the session must say so. No behaviour on any live path changes.

options.option: Delete all seven as the spec's Touches list names them.
options.consequence: Breaks the close outright: close_session imports validate_contract_gate at gate time, session_checklist imports parse_session_plans, dual_surface_verify imports validate_benchmark_registration at module scope. This is forcing unreachability by editing survivors, which the spec explicitly forbids.

options.option: Delete nothing and report the whole list as reachable.
options.consequence: Honest but wrong: four modules really are unreachable by every criterion the spec sets, and leaving them costs the maintenance the set exists to remove.

evidence: Static import graph over all 78 ai_router/*.py modules (ast, no execution): contract_gate <- __init__, close_preflight, close_session, start_session; spec_admission <- session_checklist; replacement_gate <- dual_surface_verify; floor_ratchet <- (none); pricing_proposal <- (none); routed_gate <- __init__ only; cost_report <- __init__ only.
close_session.py:2176-2262 runs read_contract_gate + validate_contract_gate and can return failed_checks=['contract_gate'] - a live close gate.
session_checklist.py:719-734 calls spec_admission.parse_session_plans to seed the plan the checklist_posted close gate reads.
dual_surface_verify.py:65,90 import validate_benchmark_registration at module scope and call it at line 1538.
router-config.yaml:995 documents routed_gate as RETIRED (Set 083) and informational only; router-config.yaml:1211 cost_report_on_exit has no reader in any ai_router module.
83 routed calls in router-metrics.jsonl carry billed_usage_unavailable: true and cost_usd: 0.0 - the cost surface a Copilot seat cannot populate.
reversal_path: git revert the deletion commit; the modules and their tests return intact, since nothing else was edited to accommodate their absence beyond the __init__ re-exports, the dead router-config keys and the doc references that named them.
